highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.148.0 is the first stable v4 release, built on Skia m148 with major font and lifecycle updates.
highlights_body: It rolls up the entire 4.147 preview line: variable fonts, animated WebP encoding, new draw and stream APIs, platform realignment, and a singleton lifecycle rework. This is a breaking release, so read the migration notes before upgrading from 3.x.

breaking.title: Legacy SKPaint text and font members are now compile errors
breaking.body: The paint text and font members that had been obsolete in v3 are now errors, and other pre-v4 obsolete members were trimmed from the reference assembly. Move typeface, text size, hinting and text encoding to SKFont and the newer SKCanvas.DrawText overloads before upgrading.

breaking.title: Vulkan YCbCr conversion types were renamed and reshaped
breaking.body: GRVkImageInfo now uses GRVkYcbcrConversionInfo, and the old GrVkYcbcrConversionInfo equality members are gone. If you construct or compare these Vulkan interop structs directly, update the type name and revisit any layout- or equality-dependent code.

breaking.title: SKNativeObject.IgnorePublicDispose no longer has a setter
breaking.body: The protected setter was removed, so subclasses can no longer flip IgnorePublicDispose after construction. If you depend on that behavior, set the intended lifetime policy during object initialization instead.

breaking.title: Default font resolution semantics changed in v4
breaking.body: Several text APIs now resolve default typefaces differently at runtime: new SKFont() starts empty, SKPaint.Typeface comes back as a usable default instead of null, and Android missing-family lookups now fall back to the default face. Audit any code that used null checks or lazy default font behavior as control flow.

breaking.title: Ganesh Vulkan now requires Vulkan 1.1
breaking.body: On Vulkan 1.0 contexts, GRContext.CreateVulkan no longer fails gracefully and can terminate the process. Create your Vulkan instance as 1.1 or later and set GRVkBackendContext.MaxAPIVersion accordingly, or choose another rendering backend on 1.0-only systems.

bullets.lead: The v4 line lands on Skia milestone m148
bullets.detail: This stable release rolls forward from the older v3 engine through the entire 4.147 preview train, picks up the m147 upstream bug-fix syncs, and ships on top of Skia m148.

bullets.lead: Variable font and color-palette support reached the managed surface
bullets.detail: SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp now expose variable-font behavior end to end, and SKFont and SKTypeface gain color font palette selection together with more robust variable-font handling.

bullets.lead: Default typeface resolution moved into managed code
bullets.detail: SkiaSharp now resolves default typefaces from the managed layer, fixing Android fallback issues and restoring the legacy typeface factory path needed by downstream callers.

bullets.lead: Surface drawing gained explicit sampling control
bullets.detail: New overloads on SKSurface.Draw and SKCanvas.DrawSurface accept SKSamplingOptions so callers can choose their filtering and mipmap behavior during surface-to-surface draws.

bullets.lead: Streams and encoders picked up new data APIs
bullets.detail: SKStream.GetData enables zero-copy conversion from a seekable stream to SKData, and SKWebpEncoder can now emit animated WebP output from a frame sequence.
The HarfBuzz binding now includes a proper HBColor value type and rounds out previously missing or inconsistently named wrapper APIs.

bullets.lead: Pixel-span access now uses the correct layout math
bullets.detail: SKPixmap and SKBitmap GetPixelSpan now honor RowBytes for stride and compute offsets from Width instead of Height, so non-tightly-packed bitmap reads return the correct pixels.

bullets.lead: SKPath finalization no longer crashes in builder-heavy code
bullets.detail: A GC ordering problem is fixed so SKPath instances created from SKPathBuilder can be finalized safely even when the builder is collected first.

bullets.lead: UI startup and rendering issues were resolved on Android and WinUI
bullets.detail: MAUI TabBar switches no longer leave Android SKGLView blank, and WinUI apps on .NET 9 can again locate the Projection assembly at startup.

Process-wide singletons such as default typefaces, font managers and related ambient objects now have a consistent managed lifetime story, reducing shutdown-time surprises and making disposal order more predictable.

bullets.lead: Native compatibility checks now run on first API use
bullets.detail: The native-library compatibility gate moved off module initialization and onto the SkiaApi type constructor, making failures easier to diagnose and avoiding module-load edge cases.

bullets.lead: Tizen, Linux Bionic and Apple targeting all moved forward
bullets.detail: The release adds Tizen x64 and arm64 support, introduces Linux Bionic native assets, and realigns Apple TFMs so libraries use versioned 26.0 targets while app projects stay on the SDK-preferred unversioned form.

bullets.lead: WASM and legacy-target support were cleaned up
bullets.detail: SkiaSharp drops native WASM builds for pre-.NET 8 Emscripten slices, while the managed layer keeps older TFMs viable with PolySharp-based C# 13 support.

bullets.lead: Bundled native dependencies were refreshed across the stack
bullets.detail: The v4 release line updates expat, libpng, zlib, freetype, libjpeg-turbo and HarfBuzz, bringing along their latest upstream security and correctness fixes in the packaged native binaries.

contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Drove the early v4 engine work, variable font support, the managed default-typeface fix, the SKPath finalizer repair, the SKPaint text/font migration, and the singleton lifecycle rework
contributor_summaries.4Darmygeometry: Added Linux Bionic native assets and PolySharp-based language support so legacy target frameworks can keep compiling with newer C# features
contributor_summaries.ebariche: Contributed Uno-side sample and integration fixes during the v4 preview cycle
contributor_summaries.sasakrsmanovic: Improved samples and related infrastructure that shipped with the v4 rollout
contributor_summaries.SimonvBez: Fixed the Android MAUI TabBar regression that left SKGLView blank after switching tabs

preview_summaries.v4.147.0-preview.1.1: Preview 1 opened the v4 line with the Skia engine jumps through m147, variable fonts, color font palettes, explicit surface sampling, managed default-typeface resolution, and the first new platform assets.
preview_summaries.v4.147.0-preview.2.1: Preview 2 added animated WebP encoding, zero-copy SKStream.GetData, the SKPath finalizer fix, and the Apple target-framework realignment.
preview_summaries.v4.147.0-preview.3.1: Preview 3 rounded out the HarfBuzz work, refreshed more native dependencies, and finalized the WASM packaging changes for the new v4 line.
preview_summaries.v4.148.0-rc.1.2: The release candidate landed the m148 engine bump, the singleton lifecycle rework, the pixel-span fixes, the WinUI .NET 9 startup fix, and the final breaking-change cleanup before stable release.

harfbuzz_summary: HarfBuzzSharp moves forward with the v4 font work, including variable fonts, HBColor, color palette support and the bundled HarfBuzz 14.2.0 refresh.
